full_judgment:
One, Chandra. Kumar Mazumder, Prashanna Kumar Mazumder, Nishi Kumar Mazumder, Shoshi Kumar Mazumder and Nakkhatra Kumar Mazumder, five full-brothers altogether got 33¾ decimals of land through auction purchase in Mortgage Execution Case No. 239 of 1934 arising out of Mortgage Case No. 366 of 1932 that comprises four different CS (DS) Khatian bearing Nos. 4, 7, 68 and 236. In an amicable partition, Nishi Kumar Mazumder among the brothers used to enjoy title and possession over that 33¾ decimals of land who during enjoying title and possession died leaving behind son, Laxmi Kanto Mazumder. While Laxmi Kanto Mazumder had been in possession of the property left by his father, Nishi Kanto Mazumder, at first sold out 33¼ decimals of land by registered sale deed dated 26-9-1973 to the said respondents and respondent No. 6 (opposite-party No. 5 to the Miscellaneous Case). Laxmi Kanto Mazumder again by registered sell deed dated 2-10-1973 also transferred 33¾ decimals of land to the same recipients. Afterwards, Laxmi Kanto Mazumder by registered sale deed dated 8-10-1973 also transferred said 33¾ decimals of land out of four different khatians in favour of the said recipients that is, respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 6 and delivered possession of the property to them. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 then on an amicable partition used to enjoy 61 decimals of land out of CS Khatian No. 68 appertaining to CS Plot No. 45. Subsequently, the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 mutated their name in the khatian and paid rent thereof. Subsequently, the respondent No. 6 (opposite-party No. 5 to the Miscellaneous Case) by an amicable arrangement transferred 33¾ decimals of land with the present petitioner (opposite-party No. 4 to the Miscellaneous Case) vide deed of exchange dated 19-5-1985. Subsequently, the opposite-party No. 4 herein the appellant transferred 15¾ decimals of land out of 33¾ decimals of land in favour of one, Abdul Motaleb. The appellant also by registered sale deed dated 3-3-1987 transferred 5¼ decimals of land in favour of one, Abdul Mannan. 

 7. The case of the predecessor of respondent Nos. 7(a) to 7(d), Akbor Hossain (opposite-party No. 6 to the Miscellaneous Case) in brief is that, Nishi Kanto Mazumder and his four full-brothers got the property to have described in the "Will" through auction purchase in execution of a decree in decree Execution Case No. 239 of 1934 on 18-4-1936 and obtained sale certificate. Nishi Kanto then disposed of his share of land through "Will" in the year 1967 and by virtue of the "Will", the executors, his two full-brothers Shashi and Nakkhatra got probate in Miscellaneous Case No. 113 of 1967 on 17-6-1969. Thereafter, Nakkhatra gifted some of his land to his son, Sanjoy Kumar Mazumder. Thereafter, Shashi Kumar, Nakkhatra Kumar also gifted lands to one, Shishir, Karuna and Shipon in the year 1973 and 1978. Then Shishir, Shipon and Karuna transferred 27 decimals of land in the year 1979 to Golam Sarwar, Golam Mohiuddin, Golam Satter and Golam Habibur Rahman. Sanjoy and Nakkhatra then transferred 27 decimals of land out of plot No. 45 to Samsun Nahar, Rawshan Ara, Salma Khatoon, Mahamuda Khatun and Mahmuda Rahman. In the aforesaid way, Rawshan and others vis-a-vis Golam Sarwar and others exchanged their said purchased properties with this opposite-party vide deed of exchange dated 5-4-1994. It has further been stated in the written objection that, the petitioners and opposite-party Nos. 4-5 possessed same interest and he has been enjoying title and possession in respect of plot No. 45 by deed of exchange and that of the land in khatian No. 39 through purchase and lease through his predecessor. It has finally been prayed to sustain the probate obtain through Miscellaneous Case No. 113 of 1967 but set-aside the letter of administration obtained on 7-3-1969 vide Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1988.
